INSTITUTIONAL

Article 16

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection (P2TP2A) or other designation as an integrated service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.

c. Educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. Fostering and enhancing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 10

The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 7 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 24

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection, empowerment of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 14

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide complaint services for the protection and empowerment of women and children.
2. The Regional Government and the community or social service institutions may establish recovery houses or safe houses.

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 21

b. Technical guidance and training;
c. Provision of facilities;
d. Monitoring; and
e. Evaluation.

4. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

FINANCING

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 21

1. The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection, empowerment of women and children.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. Guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. Technical guidance and training;
c. Provision of facilities;
d. Monitoring; and
e. Evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protection, empowerment of women and children in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD and the community.
4. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be conducted with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

Article 22

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection, empowerment of women and children organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

CHAPTER VIII

INSTITUTIONAL

Article 16

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes an Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection (P2TP2A) or other designation as an integrated service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.
2. The Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection (P2TP2A) or other designation as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as a leading sector of the integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the organization and working procedures of the Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection (P2TP2A) or other designation as referred to in paragraph (1), are stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 24

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection, empowerment of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

Article 9

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the Private Sector and society as referred to in Article 7 letter b, are carried out in the form of community participation and jointly.
2. The form of participation of the private sector and society as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:a. Preventing acts of violence against women and children; b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; andc. Participating in handling victims of acts of violence.
3. The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), is carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20

1. The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through: a. Notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. Educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. Fostering and enhancing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 14

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide complaint services for the protection and empowerment of women and children.
2. The Regional Government and the community or social service institutions may establish recovery houses or safe houses.

FINANCING

Article 23

a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBN);
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
c. Other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
